name: top4_loop04
text: # Biomedical Annotation Guidelines

name: top4_loop04
text: ## What to Annotate

name: top4_loop04
text: ### 1. Annotate all **Specific Disease** mentions

name: top4_loop04
text: A textual string referring to a disease name may refer to a **Specific Disease** or a **Disease Class**.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Disease Class**: Mentions that could be described as a family of multiple specific diseases.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Specific Disease**: Mentions that can be linked to one specific definition that does not include further categorization.

name: top4_loop04
text: **Example**

name: top4_loop04
text: > Diastrophic dysplasia is an autosomal recessive disease characterized by short stature, very short limbs and joint problems that restrict mobility.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Annotate**:

name: top4_loop04
text: - "Diastrophic dysplasia" as **Specific Disease**

name: top4_loop04
text: - "autosomal recessive disease" as **Disease Class**

name: top4_loop04
text: - "short stature" and "very short limbs" as **Disease Class**, because they are clinical signs that characterize a Specific Disease (see rule 1c)

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Do not annotate**:

name: top4_loop04
text: - "joint problems" (bare general term; see "What NOT to Annotate," item 4)

name: top4_loop04
text: **1a. Named deficiency conditions (narrowest; applied first).**

name: top4_loop04
text: A noun phrase headed by a deficiency-type noun (e.g., "deficiency," "deficient activity") is a **Specific Disease** only when it is a fixed, lexicalized name for a pathological condition.

name: top4_loop04
text: Both of the following must hold:

name: top4_loop04
text: - The deficiency term is premodified by the name of an enzyme, protein, complement component, or gene (e.g., "C7 deficiency," "glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency"), or the phrase is a short-form re-mention of such a named condition (e.g., "G6PD deficiency").

name: top4_loop04
text: - The phrase names a pathological condition that defines or causes a disease, and the document uses it as the name of that condition rather than as a paraphrase of a molecular defect.

name: top4_loop04
text: Annotate the full name, including any parenthetical enzyme abbreviation.

name: top4_loop04
text: Later coreferent short-form mentions of the same condition are also **Specific Disease**, not O.

name: top4_loop04
text: A postnominal "of" or "in" complement form (e.g., "deficiency of X," "enzyme deficiency in X") is treated as a paraphrase by default and is handled by rule 1a(i).

name: top4_loop04
text: It becomes a named label only when the document itself uses that exact form as the defined name of the condition.

name: top4_loop04
text: **1a(i). Molecular-defect paraphrases (not a disease mention).**

name: top4_loop04
text: A defect-denoting nominal ("deficiency of X," "deficiency in X," "deficient activity of X," "deficit of X") whose prepositional or genitive complement names a molecular entity (an enzyme, protein, complement component, gene product, or gene symbol) is a descriptive paraphrase of a molecular defect.

name: top4_loop04
text: It is **not a disease mention under any label**: it is not Specific Disease, and rule 1c does not annotate it as Disease Class.

name: top4_loop04
text: Instead, label the conventional disease name elsewhere in the passage, using only its canonical span, or leave the phrase O if no such name exists.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Carrier or genotype descriptors.** If the span contains a genotype or carrier-state modifier (e.g., "heterozygous," "carrier," or a count of affected relatives), exclude the span entirely, regardless of its complement.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Does not apply** when:

name: top4_loop04
text: - the defect term is part of a fixed, premodifier-form label (e.g., "C7 deficiency," "G6PD deficiency") used as a name; rule 1a governs these;

name: top4_loop04
text: - the complement is not a molecular entity, such as a nutrient, vitamin, tissue, or organism (e.g., "vitamin D deficiency," "iron deficiency anemia"); the standard Specific Disease rules apply.

name: top4_loop04
text: - The rule applies even when the disease name also appears elsewhere in the same sentence, provided the defect phrase is a free-standing paraphrase of the same content.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Negative constraints (rules 1a and 1a(i))**

name: top4_loop04
text: - *Attributive use.* When the deficiency-type word modifies a different noun, it is attributive and is annotated as **Modifier** (rule 3), not as a Specific Disease. For example, in "G6PD-deficient phenotype," "G6PD deficient" is **Modifier**. The same holds for "deficient patients." A "deficient activity of X" or "deficiency of X" phrase is not attributive, because the deficiency word heads its own phrase; it is governed by rule 1a(i).

name: top4_loop04
text: - *Negated or normal-state adjectives* ("non-deficient," "normal") do not name a disease and remain O.

name: top4_loop04
text: - *Single symptom words* (e.g., "fever") are outside this rule and follow the Disease Class convention in rule 1c.

name: top4_loop04
text: - *Measured quantities.* Deficiencies or reductions that describe a measured value in a sample, assay, or expression experiment are not named conditions and remain O.

name: top4_loop04
text: - A bare "deficiency" with no enzyme, protein, or gene complement remains a general term (see "What NOT to Annotate," item 4).

name: top4_loop04
text: **1b. Specific vs. Disease Class test (Individuated-Referent Test).**

name: top4_loop04
text: Apply this test to each disease mention used as a stand-alone reference to a condition.

name: top4_loop04
text: Attributive uses are Modifiers (rule 3) and are not tested here.

name: top4_loop04
text: Deficiency nominals decided under rule 1a or 1a(i) are not re-tested here.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **(a) Anchored → Specific Disease.** If the mention contains a proper-name, eponym, acronym, gene-symbol, or enzyme-defined anchor in its head or immediate modifier, it is a **Specific Disease**, regardless of grammatical number. Examples of anchors include "Coats disease," "Norrie disease," "Sjogren-Larsson syndrome," "SLS" (when the document defines it as a disease), and "FALDH deficiency." Organism names (e.g., "Neisseria") are not anchors (see "What NOT to Annotate," item 1). A gene symbol or enzyme name that is not part of a disease mention (e.g., "BRCA1 alterations") does not create a disease mention.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **(b) Referential role of generic pathology heads → Specific Disease.** An unanchored span whose head noun is a generic pathology, lesion, or symptom noun (e.g., "telangiectasis," "detachment," "hyperplasia," "lesion") is a **Specific Disease**, regardless of any anatomical, laterality, quantitative, or descriptive premodifiers, when it names a disease through either:

name: top4_loop04
text: - (i) co-reference with a named, eponymous, or acronym disease through a parenthetical gloss of that disease, an appositive, a "so-called" construction, or a demonstrative anaphor; or

name: top4_loop04
text: - (ii) the complement or argument of a diagnostic or etiologic predicate (e.g., "associated with," "distinguished from," "causes of," "presenting with") within a clause about one disease referent.

name: top4_loop04
text: - *Negative constraints for (b):*

name: top4_loop04
text: - If the span is one item in an enumerated list of findings, symptoms, or sequelae with no individual disease referent, it remains **Disease Class**, including bare symptom nouns in presentation lists.

name: top4_loop04
text: - A parenthetical gloss of a finding, rather than of the named disease, does not trigger (i). In "massive intraretinal and subretinal lipid accumulation (exudative retinal detachment)," the gloss describes a manifestation, so the span remains **Disease Class**.

name: top4_loop04
text: - "Characterized by" feature lists are not diagnostic predicates under (ii); they are governed by (d) and rule 1c.

name: top4_loop04
text: - An attributive premodifier role is a **Modifier** (rule 3), not a Specific Disease.

name: top4_loop04
text: - Eponyms and acronyms that stand alone as disease names remain **Specific Disease** under (a).

name: top4_loop04
text: - Bare general nouns from "What NOT to Annotate," item 4 (e.g., "condition," "disease," "disorder," "syndrome") are not pathology, lesion, or symptom heads. They remain excluded even when anaphoric (e.g., "this condition").

name: top4_loop04
text: - *Generalization note.* Premodifier shape and the lexical class of the head noun are candidate triggers for review only. They are never sufficient on their own to assign Specific Disease or Disease Class. The referential and predicate context decides.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **(c) Unanchored, individual's condition → Specific Disease.** An unanchored head noun, with or without adjectival modifiers, that names the diagnosed or presenting condition of a specific individual is a **Specific Disease**. Typical frames include a participial "presenting with" phrase, a "found to have" construction, or a clausal subject or predicate describing one patient.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **(d) Unanchored, generic frame → Disease Class.** An unanchored head noun in a generic frame is a **Disease Class**. Typical frames include a syndrome-level list of characteristic features ("characterized by") or an enumerated differential introduced by a comparative construction ("other causes of").

name: top4_loop04
text: - **(e) Default.** If none of (a)–(d) applies, decide using the Specific Disease and Disease Class definitions above.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Negative constraints**

name: top4_loop04
text: - Do not promote an unanchored term to **Specific Disease** solely because a patient appears elsewhere in the document. The clause frame containing the term governs.

name: top4_loop04
text: - Do not treat plural number or added modifiers as evidence of a Disease Class label when an anchor is present.

name: top4_loop04
text: - Adjectival modifiers (e.g., "acute," "classical," "inherited") do not by themselves change the label. The head noun and the tests above decide it.

name: top4_loop04
text: - Anchored terms that name a broad grouping of distinct disorders rather than one disease entity remain **Disease Class**.

name: top4_loop04
text: **1c. Disease-manifestation nominals (broadest; applied last).**

name: top4_loop04
text: Annotate as one **Disease Class** span a noun phrase that denotes an abnormal pathological state, developmental abnormality, clinical sign, or deficiency of a disease-relevant molecule (the last only when it is not a molecular-defect paraphrase under rule 1a(i); see exclusion (g)), when it is either:

name: top4_loop04
text: - the argument of a characterization, causation, or etiology predicate (e.g., "characterized by," "results in," "secondary to") within a clause that describes a Specific Disease, directly or through a chain of causal predicates; or

name: top4_loop04
text: - a coordinated member of such an argument list.

name: top4_loop04
text: The span includes the head, internal modifiers, and any prepositional complement, even when the phrase has no explicit disease head word.

name: top4_loop04
text: Label each coordinated member as its own span.

name: top4_loop04
text: Single-word symptoms in such a list (e.g., "spasticity") follow this rule.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example.** In "Coats disease is characterized by abnormal retinal vascular development," "Coats disease" is a **Specific Disease** (rule 1b(a)), and "abnormal retinal vascular development" is a **Disease Class**.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Does not apply when:**

name: top4_loop04
text: - (a) The phrase is itself a named disease, syndrome, or nosological label. Those follow rule 1b; for example, a disease noun such as "ichthyosis" in a "characterized by" list is handled there. The rule also does not apply to a named deficiency condition covered by rule 1a, which is narrower and takes precedence.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (b) The causal chain concerns a gene, mutation, variant, polymorphism, drug, exposure, or population rather than the disease's own abnormal state. Gene-level abnormal states (e.g., "WT1 dysfunction") and gene-level alterations (e.g., "somatic mutation") are never manifestations under this rule.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (c) The phrase is a study variable, outcome measure, assay, method, or procedure.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (d) It describes neutral physiological or molecular background outside any disease-characterizing clause, including neutral processes such as "normal retinal vasculogenesis" (see "What NOT to Annotate," item 5).

name: top4_loop04
text: - (e) It is a standalone severity, onset, or temporal qualifier (e.g., "early onset"). Such a qualifier remains a **Modifier** and is not part of a Disease Class span.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (f) It is a bare general term (e.g., "abnormalities," "complications," "problems"), which remains excluded under "What NOT to Annotate," item 4.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (g) The phrase is a molecular-defect paraphrase under rule 1a(i) (e.g., "deficient activity of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase (FALDH)," "deficiency of norrin"). Such phrases are not disease mentions under any label.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (h) The phrase is a generic pathology span that names a disease under rule 1b(b). That rule takes precedence, and the span is a **Specific Disease**.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (i) The phrase is a coordinated set of premodifiers over one shared pathological head, which is a **Composite Mention** under rule 2.

name: top4_loop04
text: ### 2. Annotate **contiguous text strings**

name: top4_loop04
text: A textual string may refer to two or more separate disease mentions.

name: top4_loop04
text: Such mentions are annotated with the **Composite Mention** category.

name: top4_loop04
text: **Example**

name: top4_loop04
text: > The text phrase "Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy" refers to two separate diseases.

name: top4_loop04
text: If this phrase is separated into two strings: "Duchenne" and "Becker muscular dystrophy," it results in information loss, because the word "Duchenne" on its own is not a disease mention.

name: top4_loop04
text: **Coordinated premodifiers over a non-disease head.**

name: top4_loop04
text: If a span contains a coordinating conjunction ("and," "or") that joins two or more premodifiers which together modify one shared head noun, and that head denotes a pathological process, finding, or change rather than a disease name or disease category, the full coordinated span is one **Composite Mention**, not Disease Class.

name: top4_loop04
text: An adjacent Disease Class mention or a parenthetical does not change this label.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example.** "Fibroepithelial or epithelial hyperplasias" (example 18).

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Does not apply when:**

name: top4_loop04
text: - (a) The coordinator joins disease-name or disease-category heads (e.g., organ-site modifiers sharing a disease-name head such as "cancer"). This coordinated-cancer case is not reclassified by this principle. Annotate the disease mention per rules 1b and 3, and keep multi-disease coordinations such as example 7 as Composite Mentions under the first paragraph of this rule.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (b) The coordinator joins separately headed noun phrases or whole disease mentions rather than premodifiers of a single shared head.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (c) The span contains no coordinator. Single-headed nominals keep their ordinary label (Disease Class or Specific Disease).

name: top4_loop04
text: ### 3. Annotate disease mentions that are used as **Modifiers** for other concepts

name: top4_loop04
text: A textual string may refer to a disease name, but it may modify a noun phrase (or may not be a noun phrase itself).

name: top4_loop04
text: In such cases, annotate using the **Modifier** category.

name: top4_loop04
text: An attributive disease mention is a **Modifier** even if it is anchored in the sense of rule 1b.

name: top4_loop04
text: The Specific Disease / Disease Class test does not override this role.

name: top4_loop04
text: **Example**

name: top4_loop04
text: > Although this mutation was initially detected in four of 33 colorectal cancer families analysed from eastern England, more extensive analysis has reduced the frequency to four of 52 English HNPCC kindreds analysed.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Annotate**:

name: top4_loop04
text: - "colorectal cancer" as **Modifier**

name: top4_loop04
text: - "HNPCC" as **Modifier**

name: top4_loop04
text: **Adjacency-based attributive test (applies to disease-name spans, full names and short-form aliases).**

name: top4_loop04
text: - **IF** a disease-name span (a full name or its short-form alias) is **immediately** followed by a common-noun head that it attributively premodifies, with no intervening punctuation, bracket, participle, finite verb, or preposition, **THEN** label the span **Modifier**.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **OTHERWISE**, label the span **Specific Disease**. This covers spans followed by punctuation, a bracket, a participle, a verb, a preposition, or nothing, and spans that head their own noun phrase, complement a preposition, or serve as a subject or verb argument. A parenthetical acronym or alias takes the class of its expanded antecedent, judged by the antecedent's syntactic position, not by the alias's own local context.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Negative constraints (the test does NOT apply when):**

name: top4_loop04
text: - The decision rests on the semantic content of the following noun (e.g., "risk," "mutation," "patients," "genes") or on other occurrences of the same string in the document. The following word may confirm that the next token is a noun head, but it cannot by itself change the label.

name: top4_loop04
text: - The span is a Disease Class mention or a Composite Mention. Those are resolved by their own definitions before this test is applied.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example.** In "a family history of ovarian cancer," "ovarian cancer" is **Specific Disease** (complement of "of," followed by punctuation). In "ovarian cancer risk," "ovarian cancer" is **Modifier** (immediately followed by a head noun).

name: top4_loop04
text: **Locus-designator heads.**

name: top4_loop04
text: A disease-denoting premodifier (a spelled-out disease name, or an acronym that the document has already defined as a disease) in attributive position within a noun phrase whose head denotes a gene or locus is a **Modifier**.

name: top4_loop04
text: A locus head is "gene," "genes," or "gene" followed by a numeral or symbol.

name: top4_loop04
text: This rule extends the adjacency test above; it does not restrict it to gene heads.

name: top4_loop04
text: The locus head does not turn the disease span into O.

name: top4_loop04
text: The locus designator and any bare gene symbol remain O.

name: top4_loop04
text: Gene symbols stay outside the schema, and the Specific Disease / Disease Class boundaries are unchanged for non-attributive uses.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example.** In "breast cancer susceptibility gene 1 (BRCA1)," "breast cancer" is **Modifier**, and "BRCA1" is O. In "SLS genes," "SLS" is **Modifier**.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Does not apply when:**

name: top4_loop04
text: - (a) The disease term is the head of the phrase, or it sits in a postmodifying prepositional phrase and is not immediately followed by a noun it premodifies (e.g., "gene for ___"). The disease is then not attributive, and the adjacency test gives **Specific Disease**.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (b) The acronym has no disease definition or established disease referent in the document, so it remains O.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (c) The span is a gene symbol or locus name containing no disease term.

name: top4_loop04
text: - (d) The premodifier is a non-disease attributive noun (e.g., anatomical, drug, or procedure terms).

name: top4_loop04
text: ### 4. Annotate **duplicate mentions**

name: top4_loop04
text: For each sentence in the PubMed abstract and title, the locations of all disease mentions are marked, including duplicates within the same sentence.

name: top4_loop04
text: ### 5. Annotate **minimum necessary span of text**

name: top4_loop04
text: Use the smallest span necessary to include all tokens expressing the most specific form of the disease.

name: top4_loop04
text: For named deficiency conditions with a premodifier enzyme, protein, or gene name (rule 1a), that name is part of this minimum span.

name: top4_loop04
text: Molecular-defect paraphrases (rule 1a(i)) are not disease mentions and are not annotated.

name: top4_loop04
text: **Example**

name: top4_loop04
text: > In the case of "insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus," the disease mention including the whole phrase was preferred over its substrings such as "diabetes mellitus" or "diabetes."

name: top4_loop04
text: ### 6. Annotate all **synonymous mentions**

name: top4_loop04
text: Abbreviation definitions such as "Huntington disease" ("HD") are separated into two annotated mentions (one for the long form, one for the abbreviation).

name: top4_loop04
text: The short form takes the class of its expanded antecedent (rule 3).

name: top4_loop04
text: ## What NOT to Annotate

name: top4_loop04
text: 1. **Do not annotate organism names**

name: top4_loop04
text: - Organism names such as "human" were excluded from the preferred mention.

name: top4_loop04
text: - Viruses, bacteria, and other organism names were not annotated **unless** it was clear that the disease caused by these organisms is being discussed.

name: top4_loop04
text: - Organism names are also not anchors for the Specific Disease / Disease Class test (rule 1b).

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example**

name: top4_loop04
text: > Studies of biopsied tissue for the presence of Epstein-Barr virus and cytomegalovirus were negative.

name: top4_loop04
text: In this case: "Epstein-Barr virus" and "cytomegalovirus" are annotated as **Specific Disease** category **only** if the context clearly indicates the diseases they cause, otherwise not.

name: top4_loop04
text: 2. **Do not annotate gender**

name: top4_loop04
text: - Tokens such as "male" and "female" were only included if they specifically identified a new form of the disease.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example**

name: top4_loop04
text: > "male breast cancer"

name: top4_loop04
text: 3. **Do not annotate overlapping mentions**

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example**: The phrase "von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease" is annotated as **one single disease mention** (Specific Disease category).

name: top4_loop04
text: 4. **Do not annotate general terms**

name: top4_loop04
text: - Very general terms such as "disease," "syndrome," "deficiency," "condition," "complications," "abnormalities," "problems," etc. were excluded.

name: top4_loop04
text: - However, the terms "cancer" and "tumor" were retained.

name: top4_loop04
text: - A bare general term stays excluded even inside a characterizing clause or as an anaphor (e.g., "this condition"). "Deficiency" and "abnormalities" qualify only as part of a specific nominal under rule 1a or rule 1c (e.g., "C7 deficiency" or "abnormal retinal vascular development"), never on their own.

name: top4_loop04
text: 5. **Do not annotate references to biological processes**

name: top4_loop04
text: - e.g. Terms corresponding to biological processes such as "tumorigenesis" or "cancerogenesis."

name: top4_loop04
text: - Neutral developmental or physiological processes (e.g., "normal retinal vasculogenesis") are excluded likewise.

name: top4_loop04
text: - An abnormal pathological state that characterizes a Specific Disease (e.g., "abnormal retinal vascular development") is not a neutral process and is handled by rule 1c.

name: top4_loop04
text: 6. **Do not annotate disease mentions interrupted by nested mentions**

name: top4_loop04
text: - Essentially, do not break the contiguous text rule.

name: top4_loop04
text: - A parenthetical gene or enzyme abbreviation inside a single name (e.g., "glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency") is not an interruption.

name: top4_loop04
text: - The contiguity constraint also applies to manifestation and deficiency spans.

name: top4_loop04
text: - **Example**

name: top4_loop04
text: > WT1 dysfunction is implicated in both neoplastic (Wilms tumor, mesothelioma, leukemia, and breast cancer) and nonneoplastic (glomerulosclerosis) disease.

name: top4_loop04
text: Here, the mentions "neoplastic disease" and "nonneoplastic disease" are not annotated because other tokens break up these phrases.

name: top4_loop04
text: 7. **Do not annotate negated or normal-state deficiency adjectives**

name: top4_loop04
text: - e.g., "non-deficient polymorphic variant G6PD A." The word "non-deficient" names no disease, so it remains O.

name: top4_loop04
text: 8. **Do not annotate gene-level alterations as disease mentions**

name: top4_loop04
text: - Mutations, polymorphisms, variants, alterations, gene-level dysfunction, and gene symbols remain O. Examples include "BRCA1 alterations," "truncating mutations," "FALDH gene," and "WT1 dysfunction."

name: top4_loop04
text: - The exception is a disease term attributive to them, which is a **Modifier** under rule 3 (locus-designator heads).

name: top4_loop04
text: 9. **Do not annotate molecular-defect paraphrases as disease mentions**

name: top4_loop04
text: - Phrases that describe a molecular defect by naming the molecule it affects, such as "deficiency of norrin," "enzyme deficiency in G6PD A-," and "deficient activity of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase (FALDH)," are O under rule 1a(i). The disease mention is carried by the canonical disease name elsewhere in the passage, if one exists.

name: top4_loop04
text: ## Precedence Between Overlapping Rules

name: top4_loop04
text: Where two rules would label the same span differently, apply the narrower rule first and treat the broader rule as excluding that span.

name: top4_loop04
text: 1. **Attributive role before label.** A disease mention used attributively is a **Modifier** (rule 3, including locus-designator heads). The Specific Disease / Disease Class test (rule 1b) does not apply to it. For other disease-name spans, the adjacency test in rule 3 is applied first; rule 1b then decides between Specific Disease and Disease Class for non-attributive mentions not already decided by rule 1a or 1a(i).

name: top4_loop04
text: 2. **Named deficiency and molecular-defect paraphrases before general terms and manifestations.** Rule 1a (a lexicalized named deficiency) yields **Specific Disease**. Rule 1a(i) (a molecular-defect paraphrase) yields no disease mention under any label. Both are narrower than item 4 and rule 1c, and rule 1c excludes both spans (rule 1c, exclusions (a) and (g)). The individual-condition frames of rule 1b(c) (e.g., "found to have") do not override rule 1a(i). Where rule 1a(i) applies, the canonical disease name elsewhere in the passage carries the mention.

name: top4_loop04
text: 3. **Referential names and named disease labels before manifestations.** Named diseases, syndromes, and nosological labels are decided by rule 1b. A generic pathology span that names a disease under rule 1b(b) is a **Specific Disease**, and rule 1c never applies to it (rule 1c, exclusion (h)). A span that merely glosses a finding of a disease is not a referential name and remains governed by rule 1c.

name: top4_loop04
text: 4. **Abnormal states before neutral processes.** An abnormal pathological state within a disease-characterizing clause is a Disease Class span (rule 1c). Neutral processes remain O (item 5).

name: top4_loop04
text: 5. **Gene-level before disease.** Gene symbols, mutations, polymorphisms, variants, and gene-level dysfunction are O (item 8) unless a disease term is attributive to them (rule 3). A molecule-level deficiency that follows from a gene mutation is governed by rule 1a or 1a(i). If it is not a lexicalized named condition, it is a molecular-defect paraphrase and is not a disease mention. It is also not a rule 1c span (rule 1c, exclusion (b)), and it remains O.

name: top4_loop04
text: 6. **Contiguity is never overridden.** Item 6 applies to every span type, including manifestation and deficiency spans.

name: top4_loop04
text: 7. **Coordinated shared-head premodifiers before manifestations.** A coordinated set of premodifiers over one shared pathological head is a **Composite Mention** under rule 2 and is excluded from rule 1c (exclusion (i)). A coordinated set joining disease-name heads is not reclassified by this item (rule 2, exclusion (a)).

name: top4_loop04
text: ## Examples

name: top4_loop04
text: 1. **"Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus"**

name: top4_loop04
